text:
AcmeInfra: We're seeing a repeatable mismatch when we fan out to two tools in parallel (search + calculator). About 1-2% of requests return the wrong tool_result mapped to the wrong tool. request_id=rbq-9f3a correlation_id=acme-778

support_ella: Thanks — sorry about that. Can you paste the request payload + request_id and approx time? We'll escalate to eng.

AcmeInfra: request_id: rbq-9f3a, time: 2026-02-18T14:03:12Z. Minimal payload we used:
```json
{"prompt":"calc+search","tools":["search","calculator"],"correlation_id":"acme-778"}
```
We got a response where the calculator output contained search text (and vice versa).

support_ella: pinging @eng_oncall_raj :eyes: — assigning this to eng-oncall to triage.

eng_oncall_raj: Can you confirm whether this is Hosted or Dedicated? Also pls include any trace IDs + full curl if possible.

AcmeInfra: Hosted (us-west-2). Trace: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/tx-5423. Also noticed a billing spike at the same minute.

dev_alex: I can reproduce locally with a small probability using this quick script. It hits the function-calling path with two parallel tools; ~1-2% of runs swap tool_result ids.
```python
import requests
payload={"prompt":"add+search","tools":["search","calculator"],"correlation_id":"acme-778"}
resp=requests.post("https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate",json=payload,headers={"Authorization":"Bearer $KEY"})
print(resp.json())
```
Example runtime log snippet we captured locally:
```text
runtime: assigning tool_result id=tr-9 to invocation seq=2
runtime: assigning tool_result id=tr-8 to invocation seq=1
```
But final envelope returned seq=1 -> tr-9, seq=2 -> tr-8 (i.e. association flipped).

sre_maria: Confirming latency spike in us-west-2 at that timestamp. Trace tx-5423 shows callbacks finishing within ~10ms of each other. Suspect a race in the result-assignment queue. Relevant runtime trace excerpts:
```text
[2026-02-18T14:03:12Z] callback_finished cid=acme-778 inv_seq=1
[2026-02-18T14:03:12Z] callback_finished cid=acme-778 inv_seq=2
[2026-02-18T14:03:12Z] result_assigned cid=acme-778 seq=2 -> result_id=tr-9
[2026-02-18T14:03:12Z] result_assigned cid=acme-778 seq=1 -> result_id=tr-8
```

eng_oncall_raj: Hypothesis: the runtime uses a shared FIFO for result envelopes instead of a per-invocation sequence key; concurrent callbacks can reorder before final assignment. Proposed fix: require each tool result to include the invocation sequence (inv_seq) in the result envelope and bind by that inv_seq on assignment. I'll prepare a small canary patch that enforces seq-based assignment and roll it to us-west-2 for 1% traffic. Need AcmeInfra OK to route ~1% of their requests to canary for validation.

AcmeInfra: OK to route 1%. Also: what about billing spike and any data integrity concerns? Did any customer data leak or get cross-associated?

support_ella: Good question — engineering: this is a routing/result-association bug only; we don't store tool outputs differently. No data is being persisted outside normal logs. Billing spike looks related to retries/backoff while the customer retried — we'll monitor. ETA: deploy canary in ~30m, monitor for 1 hour, then expand if green. We'll notify you at each step. :thumbsup:

billing_bot: Automated alert: org=acme-corp usage spike +42% at 2026-02-18T14:00Z; alert_id=bill-20260218-1

deploy_bot: Canary rollout scheduled: us-west-2 1% at 2026-02-18T14:35Z (pending metrics).

support_ella: Thanks everyone — assigning follow-ups: @dev_alex will own the patch, @sre_maria will monitor traces, I'll keep AcmeInfra updated and open a support ticket with timeline.
